map_info.name: Fold Theatre
map_info.description: The F-edge first cycle. Substrate cycles between Wolfram Rule 30, Sierpinski, and Menger sponge expressions on the same floor; subdivision intensifies where the player looks; flower-grammar paints concentric anatomy in petal/sepal/stamen/pistil colour bands; the path from spawn to teleporter is guaranteed by PATH_GUARANTEE. Same map, three foldings of the same algorithm, the same body walking through.

learning_objectives: F edge: an algorithm becomes another algorithm
Apparatus-as-phenomenon: detail arrives where attention is
Pattern-as-maze: the algorithm IS the floor plan
Part-grammar: every cube knows what it is

documentation.summary: Fold_Theatre — F-edge first cycle on the substrate
documentation.layout: Long-axis corridor 13 wide x 17 deep. Spawn at z=1 col=2 (front-left), teleporter at z=15 col=10 (back-right). Centre-floor hosts the substrate runner; substrate cycles visibility expressions, paints flower-grammar roles, subdivides at viewer attention, and guarantees the spawn-to-teleporter route via PATH_GUARANTEE.
documentation.objective: Walk from entrance to exit while the floor reorganises itself. The algorithm becoming another algorithm — formal F edge — paired with the visual-grammar argument from doc/EDGES_OF_ALGORITHM_VISUAL_SEEDS.md (Haeckel Tafel 9, Codex carousel, Hilma af Klint).
key_elements: GridSubstrateRunner with all four channels (visibility + glyph + part + colour-by-role)
PATH_GUARANTEE floor-plan mode protects walkability across all visibility expressions
Flower-grammar paints concentric anatomy on the floor
Subdivide-by-attention reveals detail where the player's gaze falls
